### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Costello syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.525)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9648002)

**Proposed mechanism:** HRAS (HGNC:4837) —INCREASES→ RAS signaling pathway (P000000000); RAS signaling pathway (P000000000) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal Ras protein and pathway signaling (HP:0033695); Abnormal Ras protein and pathway signaling (HP:0033695) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Abnormal Ras protein and pathway signaling (HP:0033695) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Activating mutations in HRAS lead to constitutive activation of the RAS signaling pathway, which underlies the shared phenotypes of intellectual disability and cardiomyopathy observed in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the HRAS gene and RAS signaling pathway are not activated in cells derived from patients with MONDO:0014297, or that the shared phenotypes arise through entirely independent molecular mechanisms. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant in HRAS (e.g., allele frequency > 0.1% in gnomAD))_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the RAS signaling pathway, which is dysregulated in both diseases due to HRAS mutations, could offer therapeutic strategies for both Costello syndrome and other related RASopathies.

#### 2. linear nevus sebaceous syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.489)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9648002)

**Proposed mechanism:** HRAS (HGNC:4835) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:map04010); NRAS (HGNC:7929) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:map04010); KRAS (HGNC:6407) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:map04010); MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:map04010) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormality of skin development (HP:0000951); MAPK signaling pathway (KEGG:map04010) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250). Activating mutations in HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS lead to constitutive activation of the MAPK signaling pathway, which in turn drives the abnormal skin development seen in linear nevus sebaceous syndrome and contributes to the neurological phenotypes, such as epilepsy, observed in some patients with RASopathies like Costello syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of activating mutations in HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS in individuals with both Costello syndrome and linear nevus sebaceous syndrome. _(variant: High frequency of pathogenic variants in HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS in the general population (gnomAD).)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the hyperactivated MAPK pathway with MEK inhibitors or other pathway modulators could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions, particularly for the developmental and potentially neurological aspects.

#### 3. Noonan syndrome  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.455)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9648002)

**Proposed mechanism:** PTPN11 (HGNC:9543) —DISRUPTS→ RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP42); SOS1 (HGNC:10724) —DISRUPTS→ RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP42); RAF1 (HGNC:9887) —DISRUPTS→ RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP42); RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP42) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP42) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Gain-of-function mutations in genes such as PTPN11, SOS1, and RAF1 lead to aberrant activation of the RAS-MAPK signaling pathway. This dysregulation impacts downstream effectors, contributing to the shared phenotypes of intellectual disability and cardiomyopathy observed in both MONDO:0014297 and Noonan syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants for MONDO:0014297 and Noonan syndrome in PTPN11, SOS1, or RAF1 result in opposite functional effects (e.g., loss-of-function vs. gain-of-function) on RAS-MAPK signaling, or that these diseases converge on entirely distinct downstream pathways unrelated to RAS-MAPK signaling. _(variant: None specified, as the causal variants are typically rare and de novo.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the RAS-MAPK pathway or its downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both MONDO:0014297 and Noonan syndrome, given their shared mechanistic underpinnings. Understanding the specific downstream consequences of pathway dysregulation in each disease will be crucial for developing precise interventions.

#### 4. RASopathy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9648002)

**Proposed mechanism:** Gain-of-function variant in MAPK1 (null) —DISRUPTS→ MAPK1 (HGNC:6871); MAPK1 (HGNC:6871) —INCREASES→ RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (R-HSA-569047); RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (R-HSA-569047) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal cellular proliferation (HP:0002166); RAS-MAPK signaling pathway (R-HSA-569047) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Gain-of-function variants in MAPK1 lead to hyperactivation of the RAS-MAPK signaling pathway, which in turn contributes to phenotypes observed in both disease A and RASopathies, such as abnormal cellular proliferation and intellectual disability.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a loss-of-function variant in MAPK1 as the sole cause for disease A, or a complete lack of shared signaling pathway dysregulation in affected individuals of both diseases. _(variant: Exome sequencing data from gnomAD showing a common pathogenic loss-of-function variant in MAPK1 at a frequency > 0.1% would challenge the gain-of-function hypothesis for disease A.)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the hyperactivated RAS-MAPK pathway could offer a common therapeutic strategy for both disease A and RASopathies, potentially through MEK or upstream RAF inhibitors.

#### 5. neurocutaneous melanocytosis  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-9648002)

**Proposed mechanism:** NRAS activating mutation (rs74828031) —DISRUPTS→ NRAS (HGNC:7929); NRAS (HGNC:7929) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (GO:0000165); MAPK signaling pathway (GO:0000165) —LEADS_TO→ Melanoma (HP:0002664); MAPK signaling pathway (GO:0000165) —LEADS_TO→ Neurocutaneous melanocytosis (MONDO:0009578); NRAS (HGNC:7929) —LEADS_TO→ Leukodystrophy (HP:0002137). Gain-of-function mutations in NRAS lead to its constitutive activation, which in turn dysregulates the MAPK signaling pathway. Aberrant MAPK signaling can contribute to oncogenesis, leading to melanoma as seen in neurocutaneous melanocytosis, and can also affect neural development, contributing to leukodystrophy in other conditions linked to NRAS dysregulation.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a patient with MONDO:0014297 (Leukodystrophy, unspecified) who carries a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in NRAS, or a patient with neurocutaneous melanocytosis (MONDO:0009578) with a homozygous loss-of-function mutation in NRAS. _(variant: rs74828031)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared NRAS-MAPK pathway dysregulation in these distinct diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies, such as MEK or ERK inhibitors, that could be beneficial for patients with either condition. Furthermore, identifying shared genetic origins can aid in differential diagnosis and genetic counseling.
